core.title: Declare the fake contract on hermetic acceptances that use fakes
core.given: An acceptance artifact with execution_kind: hermetic_integration and a non-empty permitted_fakes list
core.when: the acceptance exists or is written
core.then: Declare the full hermetic fake-contract block — exercised_boundaries, permitted_fakes, one fake_contract_fidelity entry {name, fidelity, known_gaps} per permitted fake, and live_smoke_required; the declaration IS the contract.
prefer: exercised_boundaries uses only boundary_kind vocabulary values for surfaces actually exercised.
Each permitted fake gets exactly one fake_contract_fidelity entry with matching name, fidelity and a known_gaps list.
live_smoke_required: true when a paired execution_kind: live_smoke sibling acceptance must exist under the same plan artifact; optionally add live_smoke_reason.
avoid: A permitted fake without a fidelity entry, or an entry missing name, fidelity or known_gaps.
unless: permitted_fakes is empty — the fidelity rule does not apply.
core.why: The declaration IS the contract: the fake contract is the declared fidelity contract for each permitted fake — name, fidelity and required known_gaps — so every fake (or recorded-interaction cassette) substituted for live infrastructure is recorded with its name, fidelity and known gaps.
evidence: For every name in permitted_fakes there is exactly one fake_contract_fidelity entry with name, fidelity and known_gaps (a list of strings, present).
exercised_boundaries and live_smoke_required are present; when live_smoke_required is true, a paired execution_kind: live_smoke sibling acceptance exists under the same plan artifact.
verification: Trigger scope: the check fires only when the acceptance's execution_kind is hermetic_integration and permitted_fakes is non-empty; it does not cover acceptances with another execution kind (e.g. live_smoke) or with an empty permitted_fakes list, where the fidelity rule does not apply.

The check validates presence and shape of the declared block: exercised_boundaries required, a list of boundary_kind values from the controlled vocabulary (free-text boundary names are rejected); permitted_fakes a list of names of fakes/cassettes substituted for live infrastructure (may be empty); fake_contract_fidelity required when permitted_fakes is non-empty, exactly one entry per permitted fake, each with name, fidelity and known_gaps (list of strings, required); live_smoke_required a required boolean; live_smoke_reason an optional string expected when live_smoke_required is true. The boundary_kind controlled vocabulary is method-owned (part of the acceptance-artifact schema); its enforcement stays with this rule, not with a stack profile.

When live_smoke_required is true, the paired execution_kind: live_smoke sibling under the same plan artifact is verified as part of this rule's evidence; the realization records that this sibling-existence obligation is an independent candidate for a separate rule.
Reading execution_kind and permitted_fakes requires a field-level parser of the acceptance document (a new observer); file-kind/path recognition alone does not suffice.
Satisfaction is evidenced by the stack's check for this rule passing on the acceptance; the concrete validator id is a realization detail.

fires: An acceptance has execution_kind: hermetic_integration and permitted_fakes lists one or more fakes or cassettes.
A fake or cassette is added to permitted_fakes of a hermetic_integration acceptance that previously had none.
doesNotFire: An acceptance with execution_kind: hermetic_integration and an empty permitted_fakes list (the fidelity rule does not apply).
An acceptance whose execution_kind is not hermetic_integration (e.g. live_smoke).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kind that plays the acceptance-test role, so the core's file_kind activation fact ('acceptance_test') is observable as a file kind/path in this stack.
The stack's local name for the plan artifact that groups acceptances; the core's 'under the same plan artifact' (live-smoke sibling grouping) resolves to it.

bunOnly.reason: The validator id of this single rule is a realization detail (vocabulary notProfileKeys); the core's verification names the check generically ('the stack's check for this rule passes on the acceptance').

neutralityNotes: The acceptance-document field names and values (execution_kind, permitted_fakes, fake_contract_fidelity, exercised_boundaries, live_smoke_required, live_smoke_reason, boundary_kind; hermetic_integration, live_smoke) are treated as the shared acceptance-artifact schema of the ATDD method, not stack structure, and are kept verbatim in the core; a stack spelling these fields differently would need an idiom-level mapping, for which no vocabulary key exists (none proposed because the schema is method-owned, and bun.json gives no stack variant). The boundary_kind controlled vocabulary is likewise method-owned: it governs the values of exercised_boundaries in acceptance metadata, not the concrete artifact kinds that play the boundary role (the meaning documented by roles.boundary.kinds), so it is deliberately NOT a profile key — its controlled-vocabulary requirement (free-text boundary names rejected) stays with this rule in core:verification. bun.json never enumerates the vocabulary's values; if a future stack varies them, a distinct key would have to be proposed at that point. 'DESIRED OUTCOME' is supplied via roles.plan_artifact.name; the core says 'plan artifact'. The concrete validator id (tester.acceptance-violation.hermetic-fake-must-declare-contract) and the len(permitted_fakes) > 0 trigger notation are realization details: the id is bunOnly and the trigger is restated neutrally in verification and activation. 'Fakes/cassettes' is kept as general testing vocabulary, not a stack idiom.
